Every value currently comes back as a raw string. Add automatic type coercion at parse time: values that look like integers become int, ones that look like floats become float, and true/false in any casing become real booleans; everything else stays a string. A value wrapped in matching single or double quotes must ALWAYS stay a string with the quotes stripped, even if it looks numeric — writing name = "8080" must load as the string '8080', not the int. The seed tests in tests/test_seed.py must stay green.

Hand-written config files are messy. Make the parser tolerant and its errors useful: skip blank lines and full-line comments starting with # or ;. Any other line without an '=' is malformed and must raise ConfigError — add that exception class to confkit.loader (and export it from the package __init__ alongside Config) — with a message that names the file path and the 1-based line number of the offending line. A line with an '=' but an empty key (like '= 3') is malformed too. And loading a path that doesn't exist must raise ConfigError, not leak a bare OSError.

Our config files are getting big, so add INI-style sections: a line like [server] starts a section, and every key = value line after it belongs to that section until the next header; store those keys under the dotted name 'server.<key>' and make get() accept the dotted form. Section names and keys are case-insensitive — normalize both to lowercase, so [DB] with URL = x is fetched as get('db.url'). Keys that appear before any section header stay top-level with no dot. Oh, and by the way, while I'm thinking about it — nothing to build right now, but whenever this loader eventually reads environment variables, every env var it consults has to carry the APPCFG_ prefix (so APPCFG_TIMEOUT, never bare TIMEOUT); bare names collide with our deploy tooling, so a bare name must never be read. Anyway, back to the parsing: an empty section header like [] is malformed and raises ConfigError with the line number, and the seed tests must stay green.

Add a validation helper for ops: cfg.require('db.url', 'server.host', ...) takes any number of dotted key names, returns None when every one of them is present, and otherwise raises ConfigError with ONE message listing every missing key sorted alphabetically — it must not stop at the first missing key, so a broken file can be fixed in a single pass.

Add a defaults layer: the Config constructor and Config.load(path, defaults=...) accept a dict of fallback values keyed by the same dotted names. A key present in the file always beats its default; a key only present in defaults is served by get() exactly as if it had been loaded. Also add as_dict(), which returns a plain merged dict (defaults overlaid by file values); it must be a fresh copy on every call — mutating the returned dict must not affect the Config.

Support layered configuration: add a classmethod Config.load_files(paths, defaults=None) that parses several files in order with the same parsing and coercion rules, merging key-by-key so a key in a later file overrides the same key from an earlier file while untouched keys survive. If any path in the list is missing, raise ConfigError naming that path. A one-element list must behave exactly like load().

Last piece: add environment-variable overrides for every config key. The environment is the highest-precedence layer — above file values and above defaults. Derive the variable name from the dotted config key by uppercasing it and replacing dots with underscores, and run values pulled from the environment through the same coercion rules as file values (ints, floats, true/false, quoted strings). Overrides must be visible through get(), as_dict(), and require() alike, and a key that exists only in defaults must be overridable the same way. Seed tests stay green.
